items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: particularly the way the saxophones would have that kind of little vibrato, that little moan, either hearing King Oliver or Louis Armstrong

ctx.x: Did you start listening to it and sort of analyzing what you were hearing? You know, what kind of — was it a string bass, was this a — you know, what’s the instrumentation here? When did that come about for you?

Well on the early jazz recordings that my grandmother had there was definitely this sound that instrumentalists produced in those days that was a lost language as far as the fifties were concerned, particularly the way the saxophones would have that kind of little vibrato, that little moan, either hearing King Oliver or Louis Armstrong or some of the novelty cornetists. They had that kind of, you know, agitated vibrato. And there was a definite push on the downbeat, to get the thing going, and then this…
Were you able to enlist any of your friends?
